goal: Show-me: the hook and the compelling question, the cycle card with its six named steps, then the teacher thinks aloud from a topic of their own to three research questions, sorts them thin or thick, and models the three-way sort (I know it, I need to look it up, nobody can look this up) on three questions
note: Skill card "topic, three questions, thin or thick, pick one a source can answer", held by the teacher. Hook: a close photo of a spider web with one question under it. No readiness check: every row the unit assumes was used in library grade 2, so it is retrieved on day 2. Exit ticket (about 5 minutes, all at once): label two new questions thin or thick. Neutral topic (spiders); spider pictures show webs and silk, no prey being eaten. Host: social studies grade 3 unit 1 (ss3-inquiry-questions), the same weeks, on its town topic; where both run, one class question may serve both. Stand-alone: "How do spiders catch their food?"

goal: Practice: pairs with the card sort six new questions thin or thick, then sort them again as know it, look it up or nobody can look it up, with feedback after each round
note: Opens with the five-minute retrieval task: each student writes one who, what, where, when, why or how question about a picture (g2-question-to-research, library grade 2); where many miss it, the ten-minute reteach is grade 2's show-me case. Pairs hold the card. Begun with help, owned in grade 5 (g5-research-or-guess): the look-it-up sort. Exit ticket (about 5 minutes, all at once): sort three questions three ways.

goal: Inquiry: a short background read on spiders from a source the teacher gives, one predict line, three research questions of the student's own sorted thin or thick, one picked that a source could answer, its answer found in the six-source set, a partner says it back, then the self-check
note: Card withdrawn today. Judge step: before reading, the class names who made the background passage and why (the grade 2 maker-and-purpose move, one minute). Candidates kept here: the background read at the opening (about 5 minutes) and one predict line on the question sheet, "what I think I will find" (about 2 minutes). A student who cannot think of a question chooses from three on a card. Self-check: three-face scale on the card's steps, one step done well, one thing to do differently. Working notes in the research notebook. Whose voices: the passage and pictures record their makers (C12). Spider pictures show webs and silk, no prey being eaten.

goal: End-of-unit assessment, written sitting (about 20 minutes for 30): from a new topic and a short background passage, three research questions labeled thin or thick, one circled with a line on why a source could answer it, and four one-answer sort items
note: New topic (an invented one on how birds build nests), not seen in the unit. Rubric (teacher-judged): three real research questions, labels fit, the circled question has a source-answerable reason; the four sort items are checked on the page. Taken without the card. Response time: day 5.

goal: Respond: pairs share their day 3 answers with another pair (about ten minutes), then regrouped reteach by the rubric step missed, ending with one fresh try
note: Groups from the class record sheet (APPROACH unit field 7). The reteach for a missed thin or thick label uses the day 1 show-me case; for a question no source could answer, the look-it-up sort cards.

goal: Show-me: the hook and the compelling question, then the teacher thinks aloud through scenario cards on the stop rule (close, tell, no blame), private information never typed, taking turns on a shared device, keeping a school password to oneself, an easily guessed invented password beside a harder one, and caring for books and devices
note: Skill card "stop, close, tell, no blame", held by the teacher. Sensitivity: the stop rule and privacy; the teacher page says what the adult does if an upsetting result ever appears (close it, the child tells, no blame) and points to health's steps if a child tells something worrying (APPROACH section field 1). No student types or writes personal details, even on a pretend card; no real password is ever written. No day leans on the free grades 3 to 5 digital-citizenship presentation the frame names; it is a sensitivity-read source only (browser check: its download needs a sign-in). The password pair: the harder invented password is a long string of four unrelated words; the easily guessed one is a name or a short word; no symbol-swap example (current federal guidance puts length first). Exit ticket (about 5 minutes, all at once): one new scenario card, what to do and why.

goal: Show-me: key words pulled from a research question with the small words crossed out, a key-word search of the invented printed catalog, a synonym when nothing comes back, each try written on the search plan (question, key words, where to look, what came back, next try), and the found book's area on the printed library map
note: Opens with the five-minute retrieval task: find one book from a printed title entry and say its shelf label (g2-catalog-lookup, library grade 2). The search plan model is new today. Skill card "key words, search, look, try again", held by the teacher. Candidate kept: a "can I read it? yes or not yet" tick beside "what came back" (about 1 minute; the plan's five lines stay as the model hands them to grade 4). Host: the frogs research of ELA grade 3 unit 2 (e3-short-research, weeks 8 to 16) or the magnets question of science grade 3 unit 2 (weeks 5 to 9), both in step. Exit ticket (about 5 minutes, all at once): key words and one synonym for a new question.

goal: Practice: pairs with the card run three key-word searches in the printed catalog, try a synonym when a search comes back empty, record each try on the search plan, and find each book's area on the library map
note: Pairs hold the key-word card. Paper path: the printed catalog in pairs; a school with one projector may show the invented catalog page on it. Exit ticket (about 5 minutes, all at once): fix a search plan with a missing next try.

goal: Practice: pairs answer new scenario cards with what to do and why, including a pair of invented passwords to tell apart, and run the turn routine on a pretend device card
note: Pairs hold the stop-rule card. The turn routine and every scenario rule were shown on day 6. No card asks what devices or accounts a child has at home. Exit ticket (about 5 minutes, all at once): one new scenario card. The password pair: the harder invented password is a long string of four unrelated words; the easily guessed one is a name or a short word; no symbol-swap example (current federal guidance puts length first).

goal: Inquiry: for the host question, a search plan and a key-word search of the closed catalog, the book's area on the map, the found source's page read from the closed set with its maker and purpose named, a one-line answer with its credit line, a partner share and the self-check
note: Both cards withdrawn today. Candidate kept: the teacher page gives the continuum's reason for teacher-chosen lists over free searching as the reason the class uses a closed list (no added time). Searches use the closed catalog or a teacher-checked list only, with the stop rule. Answering page for each catalog entry used (Curio Class writes all). Stand-alone: "What is on the far side of the moon?" Whose voices: the catalog entries and passages record their makers (C12). Self-check on the three-face scale. The moon source set says the far side gets as much sunlight as the near side; it is the side always turned away from Earth, not a "dark side".

goal: End-of-unit assessment, written sitting (about 26 minutes for 30): for a new research question, the key words, one synonym and a filled search plan on a new catalog page whose "where to look" line names two places, the catalog and one other kind (the reference shelf on the map); one map item, "which area holds this book?"; then four scenario cards, each answered with what to do and why
note: Rubric (teacher-judged): key words fit, synonym tried, two places named, each try recorded; the map item is checked on the page. The four scenario cards ask, one each: the stop rule; private information (a page asks for a name or a photo); the two invented passwords; turns and care of a shared device. Together they are the safe-searching check (a product standing for AASL.VI.A.1: the student says what to do and why on each card). The password pair: the harder invented password is a long string of four unrelated words; the easily guessed one is a name or a short word; no symbol-swap example (current federal guidance puts length first). Taken without the cards. Response time: day 12.

goal: Respond: regrouped reteach by the rubric step missed (key words, synonym, recording the try, or a scenario answer), ending with one fresh try
note: Groups from the class record sheet. The day's class count of students meeting each rubric step is written on the mid-year check's sheet (day 13).

goal: Mid-year course-level check, written sitting (about 22 minutes for 30): from a new topic and a short background passage, three research questions labeled thin or thick, one circled with its reason, and three know-it, look-it-up or nobody-can items
note: Week 13. Samples unit 1 on a new case (a new topic on how snails move; a different sort set from day 4). Unit 2, which ended the week before, is not re-tested: its end-of-unit result is carried unscored as a class count of the students who met each rubric step, written on this sheet. Last unit 1 sitting was week 4, so no task form repeats within two weeks.

goal: Respond: small-group reteach of the missed step from the mid-year sheet, ending with one fresh try
note: Week 14. Groups by the step missed on day 13; unit 2's groups come by name from day 11's class record sheet, and a student who missed a unit 2 step there works that step instead.

goal: Show-me: the hook and the compelling question, then the teacher thinks aloud through storm sources: primary (a photo, a weather log someone kept, a letter) or secondary (a book about it), and each one's maker and purpose
note: Skill card "first-hand or about it, who made it, why; key words in the right box", held by the teacher. Storms are kept to how they form and how people stay safe indoors; no injury or damage pictures. Social studies grade 3 unit 4 teaches primary and secondary sources the same weeks (15 to 18) on Native nations content; library borrows only the idea and runs on weather cases (K to 5 neutral rule), and whichever course comes second opens with a retrieval of the first. Exit ticket (about 5 minutes, all at once): label one new source primary or secondary and name its maker. Storm safety follows the weather service's indoor rule ("when thunder roars, go indoors"), checked at the days (browser check).

goal: Show-me: notes as key words, not copied sentences, written in labeled boxes, one box per research question or the teacher's boxes, with the reason each note goes in its box, and the main idea and a key detail of a passage named (about 10 minutes); then a think-aloud on a statement that can be checked beside an opinion, and checking a plain-truth statement in a second source (about 7 minutes)
note: Opens with the five-minute retrieval task: pick the kind of source for two questions and name the maker of one invented page (g2-kinds-of-sources, g2-who-made-it, library grade 2). The second-source think-aloud opens with the grade 2 question "two books give a different fact: what do we do?" (g2-two-books-differ). The main idea and key detail are ELA's (e3-main-idea, ELA grade 3 unit 1, weeks 1 to 8, before this unit); the show-me names them itself. Candidate kept: a note goes in only if it answers the box's question (the main idea with details, about 2 minutes). One credit line per source on the note sheet, as review of the grade 2 credit line. Exit ticket (about 5 minutes, all at once): two notes from a short passage into a given box.

goal: Practice: pairs with the card sort a six-source storm set primary or secondary with maker and purpose, with the caption card (about 8 minutes); tell a checkable statement from an opinion in two short accounts of the same storm and see that they stress different facts (about 6); check where two sources differ in a second one (about 3); take notes in boxes from one passage (about 7)
note: Opens with the retrieval task: sort four fact cards into two given boxes (g2-fact-sort, library grade 2, about 3 minutes). Every move was shown on days 15 and 16. Candidate kept: the photo-and-caption item (does the caption fit the photo?) as one card of the sort. The diagram and the captioned photo, which can fairly be read either way, are discussed in the sort and not marked. The notes from one passage are collected as the day's exit evidence in place of a separate exit ticket (about 27 minutes in all).

goal: Inquiry: for the host question, choose sources from the set, a short search plan as review, notes in boxes with a credit line for each source, a pair share of a brief answer from the notes, and the self-check
note: Card withdrawn today. Host, in step: the habitat question of science grade 3 unit 4, "Surviving where you live" (s3-habitat-survival, weeks 15 to 20): a field log, a photo with caption and a book passage on how a plant or animal meets its needs in a place; the case set keeps to needs and habitats, never a hunt or predation picture. Stand-alone: "What happens in a thunderstorm?" Candidate kept: one "question I still have" line under each box (about 2 minutes; it feeds unit 4's answered-or-not line). Whose voices: the sources record their makers (C12).

goal: End-of-unit assessment, written sitting (about 27 minutes for 30): a new four-source pond-life set, each source labeled primary or secondary with its maker and purpose, one claim checked in a second source, "circle the two sources you would use for this question and say why each earns its place", then notes from one new passage into the student's two question boxes, with one "why this box" line
note: The four sources are clear-cut kinds only: a photo the maker took, a log, a letter and a book passage; their labels, makers and purposes are one-answer items. The media-accuracy item asks only whether a caption fits its photo, not the photo's kind. Choice rubric: two sources circled, each with a reason tied to the question. Notes rubric (teacher-judged): key words not sentences, each note in a box that fits, the "why this box" line, a credit line. This pond set shares no source with unit 4's team pond set. Pond life keeps to plants and small animals; no predation pictures. Taken without the card. Response time: day 20.

goal: Respond: regrouped reteach by the step missed (source kind, maker and purpose, the second-source check, or notes in boxes), ending with one fresh try
note: Groups from the class record sheet. No readiness check before unit 4: every row it assumes was used in library grade 2 and is retrieved on days 22 and 23.

goal: Show-me: the hook and the compelling question, then the team meeting modeled with a sample team: each member has a subquestion, reports one finding in turn, names what a teammate added, and the recorder writes who added what on the team sheet
note: Skill card "report, record, product from notes, source list, two notes", held by the teacher. The team turn is ELA's collaborative discussion (e3-discussion, ELA grade 3 unit 1, weeks 1 to 8, before this unit); the show-me models the team turn itself. Teams of four or five (seven teams for 30), mixed by the teacher, never by background. Exit ticket (about 5 minutes, all at once): name what a sample teammate added. The team meeting opens with SEL's four talk turn steps in SEL's words (listen, say back, ask a question, add your idea); library adds: report one finding, name what a teammate added, the recorder writes it. Where the school runs SEL it is a reminder; where it does not, this day teaches it. No time added.

goal: Inquiry: each member finds facts on their subquestion from the team pond source set, with notes in boxes and a short search plan as review; the last five minutes are a practice team meeting, one round, no score
note: Opens with the five-minute retrieval task: name what each of three sample team members added (g2-group-research, library grade 2). Host: the speaking-reports work of ELA grade 3 unit 3 (e3-speaking-reports, weeks 17 to 24) or the freshwater research of ELA grade 3 unit 4 (weeks 24 to 32); stand-alone: "What lives in a pond, and how do they depend on each other?" Pond life keeps to plants and small animals; dependence is shown as shelter, plants and clean water, with no eating pictures.

goal: Observed team meeting: each student reports one source-supported finding and names one thing a teammate added; the teacher scores two results per student, about 3 minutes a team, seven teams, about 21 minutes
note: End-of-unit evidence, part 1 of 2: the team skill, observed (an observed performance standing for both codes, scored separately; the recorder's sheet supports it and replaces neither). Taken without the card. While the teacher sits with one team, the waiting teams work a two-part card: first the retrieval, a credit line for one cover (g2-credit-line) and say back what one sample poster teaches (g2-research-share), about 5 minutes; then "finish your subquestion notes from day 22 and star the one fact you will report, with its source", about 10 minutes, which also readies the product on day 24. Eight minutes hold set-up and the exit ticket. The day 28 sitting reuses this record and does not observe again.

goal: Show-me with practice: a product (a short report, a labeled diagram or a fact poster) built only from notes, the answered-or-not line, the source list from the model card (title, author, year, kind, in that order), then pairs fix two sample source lists
note: Candidates kept: the class reads the product rubric beside a sample before drafting, as what makes a good product (about 4 minutes); the main idea with supporting details and the conclusion on whether the question was answered sit in the rubric's answered-or-not line (no added time). The product may be written or drawn; the spoken report is ELA's. Exit ticket (about 5 minutes, all at once): fix one source list.

goal: Inquiry: each student drafts a product that answers their subquestion from their notes only, with the answered-or-not line, a look-back line on one step of the search, and a source list in the model's order
note: Card withdrawn today. Candidate kept: an unscored "check before you hang it" line, "is my main point easy to find?" (presenting so main points are clear, about 1 minute). Honest use without shaming: a student whose product copies a sentence is helped privately to put it in their own words and credit it, never named in front of the class. Begun here, owned in grade 5 (g5-search-log-look-back): the look-back line.

goal: Gallery walk: the teacher models the two notes (5 minutes), pairs practice them on a sample product with the card and feedback (6 minutes), then each student writes two notes without the card on one assigned classmate's product (12 minutes); slips collected and the self-check (6 minutes)
note: The two notes: one thing the work taught, in the student's own words, and one specific, kind suggestion tied to the skill card. Partners assigned so every product gets notes (30 notes of each kind). Peer feedback is ELA's (e3-writing-process, ELA grade 3 unit 1, before this unit); the gallery models the two notes itself. The teacher reads every slip before day 27; notes stay kind and about the work. Self-check on the three-face scale.

goal: Respond to the gallery notes: each student revises the product from the notes they received, checks the source list against the model, and hands in the revised product
note: The revised product is collected and scored on its rubric (answers the subquestion, only facts from the notes, the answered-or-not line, the source list in order) as part of the end-of-unit evidence reported on day 28. The unit's regrouped reteach is on day 30.

goal: End-of-unit assessment, written sitting, all at once (about 22 minutes): a source list for three new covers in the model's order (about 8 minutes), one one-answer item, "A classmate copied a sentence from a book into their poster. What should they do?" (put it in their own words and credit it, about 2 minutes), and two gallery notes on a new sample product (about 12 minutes); with the day 23 observation and the revised product
note: End-of-unit evidence, part 2 of 2. The sitting asks for each code it lists: the source list and the copied-sentence item (VI.B.2, both parts: name who made each work and respect their rights), the learned note (I.C.1) and the suggestion (I.C.2); I.B.3 is the revised product from day 27 and III.D.1 and II.A.1 the day 23 observation, carried, not collected again. Taken without the card. Response time: the year-end check's respond day (day 30).

goal: Year-end course-level check, written sitting (about 27 minutes for 30), drawing its items from units 1 to 3: one research question with its thin or thick label; key words, a synonym, a two-try search plan on a new catalog page whose second try is in another kind of source, and two scenario cards; three sources labeled primary or secondary with maker and purpose, one second-source item (does the second source agree?), and notes from a short passage into two given boxes with one "why this box" line
note: Week 29. If the sitting runs long, drop one of the three source labels (about 25 minutes). The labeled sources are clear-cut kinds only (a photo the maker took, a log, a letter, a book passage). New cases throughout (an invented question on how bees find flowers; a new catalog page; a new source set on autumn leaves). Unit 4, which ended in week 28, is not re-tested: its results are carried unscored as a class count on the sheet. Last sittings of these forms: weeks 11, 13 and 19, so none repeats within two weeks.

goal: Respond: about 12 minutes of regrouped reteach from the unit 4 product rubric and team observation, about 12 from the year-end items, each ending with one fresh try, and about 5 for the year's reflect step
skills: g3-make-product; g3-research-team; g3-gallery-feedback; g3-research-questions; g3-key-words; g3-source-kinds-and-makers; g3-notes-in-boxes
note: Week 30. Reflect step: each student writes one thing they would like to learn more about and one step they now do well, and the class shares its products once more.
